While a knob turns, the screen shows its value as a large dial for a second.

Tracks and sounds

Six tracks, each with its own machine, sound, octave, level, pan, steps and loops. Each track keeps a sound for each of the four machines, so turning PRESETS back finds the sound it had. The tracks share twelve voices; when all twelve sound, a new note takes the quietest one. DRUM tracks choke: each hit fades the track's previous one.

The FM-1's second processor core plays half the voices and the effects. If it ever faults, the first core carries on alone until the FM-1 is switched off, and the screen says 1 CORE.

Sounds

HOME draws a new sound for the chosen track from a recipe of its machine: a family such as TIGHT KICK, METAL HAT, FM BASS or SWARM DRONE, leaning each time towards industrial, IDM or abstract. SHIFT + HOME draws another from the same family; SHIFT + PRESETS moves to the family before or after. The screen shows the machine and the family. There are 56 families: 29 for DRUM, 9 for 4-OP, 10 for WAVY, 8 for HIVE. Drone, pad and texture families come with LFOs already set.

The sound's pages (EDIT)

Black key 10 (EDIT) shows the sound's pages: SYN 1 to 4 (the machine's), FLTR 1, FLTR 2, AMP, FX and MANGLE. Each page has eight parameters: KNOB 1–4 set A to D; PRESETS turned right shows E to H, left goes back. OCT− / OCT+ move between the pages. EDIT again leaves.

4-OP

Four-operator FM after the Digitone II's FM TONE: operator C and the modulators A, B1 and B2.

PageParameters
SYN 1ALGO (eight algorithms), RATIO C, RATIO A, RATIO B, HARM, DETUNE, FEEDBACK, MIX
SYN 2the A and B envelopes: ATK, DEC, END, LEV for each
SYN 3DELAY, TRIG and RESET for A and for B, PHASE RST
SYN 4OFS C, OFS A, OFS B1, OFS B2 (fine offsets), KEYTRK A, KEYTRK B1, KEYTRK B2

DRUM

Three-operator FM percussion after FM DRUM.

PageParameters
SYN 1TUNE, SWP TIME, SWP DEPTH (the pitch sweep), ALGO (seven), OP C WAVE, OP AB WAVE, FEEDBACK, FOLD
SYN 2RATIO, DEC, END and MOD for A and for B
SYN 3HOLD, DECAY (the body), PHASE C, LEVEL, AB NOISE, NOISE RST, NOISE RM
SYN 4NS HOLD, NS DECAY, TRANS (the transient's kind), TRANS LEV, NS BASE, NS WIDTH, NS GRAIN, NS LEVEL

AB NOISE mixes operators A and B towards a noise that follows their pitch: at 0 the waveform only, at 127 the noise only. Modulating C, it gives metallic, grainy hits. With NOISE RST on, every hit gets the same noise.

WAVY

Two wavetable oscillators with phase distortion, and a noise generator.

PageParameters
SYN 1TUNE, WAVE, PD and LEVEL for each oscillator
SYN 2OFS 1, TABLE 1, MOD (OFF, RING, RING FIX, SYNC), RESET, OFS 2, TABLE 2, DRIFT
SYN 3NS ATK, NS HOLD, NS DECAY, NS LEVEL, NS BASE, NS WIDTH, NS TYPE (GRAIN, TUNED, S+H), NS CHAR

HIVE

A swarm of six detuned oscillators and a main oscillator.

PageParameters
SYN 1TUNE, SWRM WAVE, DETUNE, MIX, MAIN OCT (−2, −1, 0), MAIN WAVE, ANIMATION, NOISE MOD

FLTR, AMP, FX and MANGLE

These pages are the same on every machine.

PageParameters
FLTR 1the filter's envelope (ATTACK, DECAY, SUSTAIN, RELEASE), FREQ, RESONANCE, the filter's own parameter, ENV DEPTH
FLTR 2FLT DELAY, KEYTRACK, BASE and WIDTH (a base-width filter), BW ROUTE (before or after), ENV RESET, FILTER
AMPATTACK, HOLD, DECAY, SUSTAIN, RELEASE, RESET, MODE (AHD or ADSR), VOLUME
FXBIT REDUCE, OVERDRIVE, SRR (sample-rate reduction), OD TYPE, the DELAY, REVERB and CHORUS sends, OD ROUTE
MANGLEDESTROY and DST MODE, SLICE, SLICE RATE, SLC DEPTH, SLC EDGE, SLC SHIFT
  • FILTER: MULTI (multimode), LP4 (4-pole low-pass), LEGACY (low- or high-pass), COMB−, COMB+, EQ.
  • OD TYPE: VALVE (two valve-style stages), RAT (a RAT-style clipper, darker as it rises), FOLD (a wavefolder, which bites only once the signal is loud). RAT and FOLD come from the LXR firmware.
  • DESTROY breaks the sound digitally; DST MODE chooses how: WRAP, XOR, FLIP, DROP.
  • SLICE is a gate in time with the tempo: sixteen patterns at 1/8, 1/16, 1/32 or 1/16 triplets, with its depth, edge and shift.

Keys and scales

The white keys play the chosen track in the scale: the first key is the root, each key the next degree. The keys that play the root glow dimly. USB and TRS MIDI notes play the chosen track as the keys do (MIDI).

Scales

ARP opens the SCALE page: SELECT sets the root, ALGORITHM the scale. ARP again, or a track button, leaves it. SHIFT + ARP draws a scale and a root at random and shows them for 1.5 s over any page. The scale and root belong to the session; they can also be set on the session's page. A new session draws them at random.

The scales: CHROMATIC (the black keys play too, except the first five and the last three), MAJOR, MINOR NATURAL, MINOR HARMONIC, DORIAN, PHRYGIAN, MINOR PENTA, MAJOR PENTA, WHOLE TONE, JAPANESE IN, MINOR MELODIC, ENIGMATIC, LYDIAN, MIXOLYDIAN, LOCRIAN, BLUES, HUNGARIAN MINOR, DOUBLE HARMONIC, PHRYGIAN DOMINANT, JAPANESE HIRAJOSHI, JAPANESE IWATO, PELOG, OCTATONIC, PROMETHEUS.

Transposition

In the step view, OCT− / OCT+ move the chosen track's steps and loops one step of the scale down or up (in CHROMATIC, a semitone). SHIFT + OCT− / OCT+, in the track's view or the step view, move every track's. Notes stay in the scale. The transposition shows at the top right, under the octave (T+2, T−1), up to 24 steps each way. It is part of the pattern: saved with it, and copied with it. It moves only the loops of the pattern playing; a loop being recorded is left as it is. The keys' octave does not change.

CHORD mode

Black key 1 turns CHORD mode on or off for the chosen track (lit while on). Each white key then plays a chord from its note, in the scale. SHIFT + black key 1 chooses the next form: TRIAD, INV 1, INV 2, SUS2, SUS4, OPEN, FOURTHS. The form shows at the top left. Steps, recording and the looper take the chords. DRUM tracks play no chords.

Arpeggiator

Black key 5 turns the chosen track's arpeggiator on or off (lit while on; ARP shows at the top left). The keys held, and MIDI notes for the track, then play one at a time on the tempo's grid: with the sequencer's 16ths while it plays, on their own at the tempo while it is stopped. With CHORD mode on, each key gives it the chord's notes.

Hold black key 5 (0.8 s) to open or close the ARP page (KNOB 1–4 rows A to D; PRESETS right, E to H):

RowWhat it sets
MODEUP, DOWN, UP DOWN, DOWN UP, ORDER (as played), RANDOM, CONVERGE (from the ends in), DIVERGE (from the middle out), PINKY (the top note between each of the others), THUMB (the lowest between each)
RATE1/32, 1/16T, 1/16, 1/8T, 1/8, 1/4
RANGE1 to 4 octaves
GATEeach note's length, 0 to 100
LATCHon: the notes keep playing with the keys up, until the next chord
DENSITYthe chance that each note plays, 0 to 100
OCT RNDthe chance that a note jumps an octave, 0 to 100
BASSOFF, or EVERY 2 to EVERY 8: every so many notes, the lowest an octave down

REC records the arpeggio into the steps and SHIFT + REC into a loop; with either armed, its first note starts the sequencer. The arpeggiator and its settings are saved with the session and the pattern.

MUTE mode

Black key 2 turns MUTE mode on or off (lit while on; the screen reads MUTE MODE). The track buttons then mute instead of choosing:

ToDo this
Mute a track, or bring it backpress its button (lit: playing; dim: muted)
Solo a trackhold its button 1 s
End the solohold it 1 s again: the mutes come back as they were

A muted track fades out, its sends with it; its steps keep running silently. The mutes stay when MUTE mode is turned off. They are saved with the pattern. MUTE mode also works on the PATTERNS grid.

BREAK

While the sequencer plays, hold black key 3 to break up the chosen track's pattern; SHIFT + it, every track's. Nothing is written into the steps: when the key is let go, the pattern carries on from where it would have been.

Each press draws one way of playing the steps, shown on the screen, and keeps it while the key is held. The break starts on the track's next beat, and what is on a beat stays on a beat:

WayWhat plays
REPEAT 1, 2, 4 or 8a window of that many steps, played over and over
HALF TIMEthe steps at half speed
DOUBLEthe steps at double speed
REVERSE 4 or 8each window of 4 or 8 steps backwards, its first step in place
CHOPthe bar's four beats shuffled, the first in place
ROLLthe steps as written, with more ratchets

On top of the way, a break may add ratchets (faster the longer the key is held), flams on drums, octave leaps on melodic tracks, a gap at the end of each bar, and accents. A kick keeps the bar's first step and takes no leaps; drones are left alone; loops play on as recorded.

Saving a break. BREAK also works on the PATTERNS grid. There, with black key 3 held and the sequencer playing, hold a white key 0.8 s: the break, as it plays, is saved into that pattern slot (BREAK SAVED, PATTERN n). The pattern playing goes on.

The effects (SEQ)

SEQ shows CHORUS, COMP, DELAY and REVERB, then the chosen track's LFO 1, LFO 2 and LFO 3, in turn, then goes back. OCT− / OCT+ move between them. KNOB 1–4 set the first four rows; PRESETS turned right shows the next four. A track button goes back to the track; SHIFT + a track button chooses another track and stays on the page.

PageRows
CHORUSDEPTH, SPEED, HPF, WIDTH, DELAY (its send to the delay), REVERB, VOLUME
COMPthe master compressor: THRESHOLD, ATTACK, RELEASE, RATIO, MAKEUP, MIX; then the chosen track's SC SOURCE and SC LEVEL
DELAYTIME (in time with the tempo), PING PONG, WIDTH, FEEDBACK, HPF, LPF, REVERB, VOLUME
REVERBPRE, DECAY, FREQ, GAIN (the high shelf), HPF, LPF, VOLUME

Sidechain

On the COMP page, SC SOURCE chooses the track whose hits duck the chosen track (OFF: none) and SC LEVEL how deep, 0 to 100; at 100 the track is all but silenced on each hit. The duck lets go at the compressor's RELEASE, and the track's effect sends duck with it.

LFOs

Each sound has three LFOs, on the pages LFO 1 to 3. They belong to the sound, so each machine's sound on a track has its own, and they are saved with the session. All of a track's voices follow the same LFO.

RowWhat it sets
SPEED−64 to +63; negative runs the wave backwards. SPEED +32 with MULT x4 is one bar
MULTx1 to x2048 follow the tempo; .1 to .2048 run as at 120 BPM whatever the tempo
FADE0 none; negative fades the LFO in, positive fades it out, from each note
DESTNONE, or a parameter of the sound's pages (S1–S4, F1, F2, AMP, FX, MNG). LFO 2 can also move LFO 1's SPEED or DEPTH, and LFO 3 those of LFO 1 or 2
WAVETRI, SINE, SQR, SAW, EXP, RAMP, RND (a new random value each cycle)
STARTwhere the wave starts on a note. For RND: how smoothly it moves to each new value
MODEFREE runs on; TRIG starts again on each note; HOLD holds its value from each note to the next; ONE runs one cycle from each note; HALF half a cycle
DEPTH−64 to +63, how far each way; negative turns the wave upside down; 0 off

SHIFT + SEQ draws the chosen track's three LFOs anew (LFO RANDOM): two or three of them on, each to a different parameter, with any wave, speed, mode and depth. It takes risks on purpose: press it again for another. LFO settings cannot be step-locked.

The sequencer

Each track has 16 steps, with its own length (1 to 16), clock (1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1X, 2X, 4X) and direction. PLAY starts and stops it.

The step view

Black key 9 (STEP) turns the step view on or off. The white keys are then the chosen track's 16 steps: lit, a note; dim, empty; the step playing the other way round; past the track's length, dark. Steps are silent while you edit them.

ToDo this
Put a note inpress an empty step: the track's last note (or chord) goes there
Empty a steppress a step with a note, and let go
Lock a value on a stephold the step and turn KNOB 1–4 (filter, sends), SELECT (level) or ALGORITHM (pan)
Lock a sound parameterhold the step with the EDIT pages up and turn a knob; up to eight locks a step
Copy a stepSHIFT + hold it 0.8 s (COPY blinks)
Paste itSHIFT + hold another step 0.8 s, on this track or another
Empty the whole trackSHIFT + STEP (with the step view on or off): its steps and locks; the rest of the track is kept

The black keys, lit dimly, do this in the step view:

KeyWhat it does
black key 1a new phrase for the track. SHIFT +: new locks on its steps. Held (0.8 s): the PHRASE page
black key 2the TRACK page: LENGTH and CLOCK
black key 3TRIG on or off: a step held shows its own page
black key 4MOD on or off: a step held shows its MOD page
black keys 6, 7, 8the track's direction: REVERSE, PING-PONG, RANDOM; pressed again, forwards

A step's own pages

TRIG: KNOB 1 the step's note (in the scale), 2 its velocity, 3 its length, 4 its trig condition; with PRESETS turned right, KNOB 1 its RATCHET (the step played 2 to 8 times). The conditions are the Digitone II's: PRE and !PRE (as the last condition was met or not), NEI and !NEI (as the track before met its condition), 1ST and !1ST (the first time through), probabilities, and A:B (the A-th time of every B).

MOD: KNOB 1 MUTATE (the note moved by up to N steps of the scale, or RND), 2 MUT EVERY (how often), 3 MIDI FX (ECHO, ECHO UP, ECHO DN, STUTTER, FLAM, LATE, GRACE, FIFTH, TRIAD, OCT UP, OCT DN, DROP), 4 FX EVERY.

Phrases

In the step view, black key 1 writes a new phrase for the chosen track: steps, notes, velocities, lengths, conditions, ratchets and locks, made for the role of its sound (KICK, SNARE, HAT, PERC, NOISE, BASS, LEAD, STAB, DRONE). On the PHRASE page, DENSITY and COMPLEXITY (0 to 100) thin it out or fill it.

Recording

REC records the keys into the chosen track's steps, each note with its velocity and length, until REC again. Stopped, REC arms (it flashes, the metronome counts in) and the first note starts the sequencer. SHIFT + PLAY turns the metronome on or off.

The looper

SHIFT + REC arms a loop on the chosen track; the first note starts it (and the sequencer, if stopped). REC ends it. Its length is rounded to whole bars (1 to 32), so it stays in time with the steps (LOOP 1 4 BARS shows). Three loops a track, up to 256 notes each.

ToDo this
See the track's loopshold SHIFT + REC: they show on the first three white keys (lit: playing; dim: muted)
Mute a loop, or bring it backwith SHIFT + REC held, press its key
Empty one loopwith SHIFT + REC held, hold its key 0.8 s
Empty all the track's loopshold SHIFT + REC 1.5 s without touching a key

A loop belongs to the pattern it was recorded in. Another pattern does not play it, and an empty pattern plays nothing. When a pattern comes in, its loops start with its steps. Saving, copying or pasting a pattern takes its loops along; emptying it removes them. All patterns share room for 40 loops and 4608 notes: when it is full, arming a loop shows NO ROOM, and a pattern saved into another slot shows LOOPS LOST for the loops that did not fit.

Tempo

Hold PLAY (0.8 s) for the TEMPO page: PRESETS sets the session's tempo, 10 to 300 BPM. A track button leaves it.

Patterns

A session has 16 patterns. A pattern holds every track's steps (with their length, clock, direction and transposition), its loops, and each track's mute, machine, octave, level, pan, sidechain, CHORD mode and arpeggiator. The sounds, the effects, the tempo, the scale and the root belong to the session.

SAVE opens the PATTERNS grid; SAVE again leaves it. The white keys are the 16 patterns, the one playing brighter. On the screen the pattern playing is green (orange with changes not saved), saved patterns white, empty ones grey, and the white square is the cursor: it opens on the pattern playing, and PRESETS moves it.

ToDo this
Play a patternpress and release its white key. While the sequencer plays, it starts at the end of the chosen track's steps
Save the pattern playing into a slothold the slot's white key 0.8 s, or move the cursor there and hold SAVE; the slot may be empty or not, and the pattern playing goes on
Save its changes in its own slothold its own white key 0.8 s
Copy a patternSHIFT + hold its key 0.8 s
Paste itSHIFT + hold another key 0.8 s
Empty a patternhold SHIFT and black key 1, and press its key
Leave the gridSAVE, or a track button

A changed pattern keeps its changes when you switch away, until the session is saved or loaded. A pattern that unmutes a track starts that track cleanly, without notes left over from the muted time. Every note is always saved; on a pattern crowded with locks, the last locks may be left out. MUTE mode and BREAK work on the grid too, and MIDI program changes 0 to 15 choose patterns 1 to 16 (MIDI).

Sessions

16 sessions are kept in the FM-1's flash. A session holds everything: every track's sounds and settings, the effects, the tempo, the scale and root, the 16 patterns with their loops, and the pattern playing.

SHIFT + SAVE opens the SESSIONS list; SHIFT + SAVE again leaves it. PRESETS chooses a slot and SAVE opens its page: BACK, LOAD, SAVE, COPY, DELETE, TEMPO, ROOT, SCALE. SAVE runs the row chosen, or moves to its value (PRESETS changes it, SAVE sets it, SHIFT + SAVE leaves it as it was). Loading over changes not saved, saving over another session, copying over one and deleting ask first: NO or YES on PRESETS.

ToDo this
Save the session playinghold SAVE (or HOME) 0.8 s, away from the SESSIONS pages and the PATTERNS grid. Never saved, it offers the first empty slot (SAVE NEW?)
Load a sessionits page, LOAD
Start a new sessionSAVE on an empty slot's page: new sounds, a scale and root at random, tempo 120, no patterns or loops. It asks first if the session playing has changes not saved. With nothing saved yet, it saves what is playing there instead
Copy a session into another slotits page, COPY, then the slot
Delete a sessionits page, DELETE

Loading a session brings all of it back; while the sequencer plays, its loops start at the next bar. Loops take room in a store shared by all the sessions: if it is full, NO ROOM FOR LOOPS shows and nothing is saved; deleting a session frees room. Sessions saved by older builds load as they played. Changes not saved before the FM-1 is switched off are lost.

How the FM-1 starts is set in GLOBAL SETUP > START: with a new session (NEW) or the last session loaded or saved (LAST).

Backup

The website's Backup page (desktop Chrome, Edge or Opera, over USB MIDI) copies every session, with its patterns and loops, and GLOBAL SETUP to a file on the computer, and writes them back. Use it before installing another firmware: Bigorna keeps its sessions where Tonitor keeps its own, so either may overwrite the other's. A restore puts each session back into its own slot and leaves the others; RESTORED S3 (or SETUP) shows as each lands.

GLOBAL SETUP

SHIFT + SAVE held (0.8 s) opens GLOBAL SETUP: the FM-1's own settings, kept apart from the sessions. PRESETS moves through the entries; SAVE opens one, or moves to a value and sets it; SHIFT + SAVE leaves a value as it was or goes back a level. A track button leaves. Changes are saved as you leave.

START: how the FM-1 starts. NEW (at first): with a new session, as Tonitor starts: new sounds on every track, a scale and root at random, tempo 120. Hold SAVE to keep it. LAST: with the last session loaded or saved.

MIDI

MIDI goes over the USB cable both ways (the FM-1 shows up as FM-1 Bigorna) and comes in through the 3.5 mm MIDI IN jack (TRS Type A). The settings follow the Model:Cycles' MIDI CONFIG:

PartSettingsAt the start
SYNCCLK IN: follow a MIDI clock and its transport; CLK OUT: send them; PCH IN: a program change chooses the pattern; PCH OUT: send one when a pattern is chosen (ON / OFF)all OFF
IN CHANTRACK 1 to 6: the channel each track listens on; AUTO: the channel that plays the chosen track; PCH: the program changes' channel1 to 6; AUTO 16; PCH 16
OUT CHANTRACK 1 to 6: the channel each track sends on; PCH1 to 6; PCH 16
RECEIVENOTES, CC (ON / OFF)ON, ON
SENDNOTES, CC (ON / OFF)OFF, OFF
PORTSUSB IN, TRS IN: take MIDI from USB, from the jack (ON / OFF)ON, ON

Clock in. With CLK IN on, the FM-1 follows the clock that arrives: its tempo, START (from step 1), CONTINUE (from the song position) and STOP. The sending device must send its transport as well as its clock (on Elektron machines, CLOCK SEND and TRANSPORT SEND). The TEMPO page shows EXT TEMPO. If the clock stops for half a second, the FM-1 goes back to its own tempo.

Clock out. With CLK OUT on, the FM-1 sends its clock all the time, so another device can lock to it before it starts; PLAY sends START, stopping sends STOP.

Notes. A note on a track's IN channel plays that track; on the AUTO channel, the chosen track. Notes on the chosen track are recorded as the keys are. With SEND NOTES on, every note a track plays (steps, loops, keys, notes received) goes out on its OUT channel; a muted track sends nothing.

CCs. Each track answers to, and with SEND CC sends, these CCs on its channel: level 7, pan 10, mute 94 (64 and up mutes), and each page's eight parameters (A to H), whatever the machine:

PageABCDEFGH
SYN 11617181920212223
SYN 22425262728293031
SYN 33334353637394041
SYN 44243444546474849
FLTR 15051525354555657
FLTR 25859606162637071
AMP7273747576777879
FX8081828384858687
MANGLE88899091929395102

Program changes 0 to 15 choose patterns 1 to 16, in time as the PATTERNS grid does.

The jack takes everything USB does except SysEx. With both inputs on they are merged; a clock should come from only one of them. A controller cannot be plugged straight into the FM-1's USB-C port (both are USB devices and need a computer between them); one with a 5-pin MIDI OUT goes into the jack.

Tested with:

  • Elektron Digitone II, into the TRS jack (a Roland TRS-to-DIN cable, Type A): the FM-1 follows its clock, starts and stops with it, and its keyboard plays the FM-1's tracks by channel. On the Digitone II, in SETTINGS > MIDI CONFIG: SYNC > CLOCK SEND and TRANSPORT SEND on; PORT CONFIG > OUTPUT TO MIDI (or MIDI+USB), TRIG KEY DEST INT + EXT, OUTPUT CH TRK CH (or AUTO CH). On the FM-1: GLOBAL SETUP > MIDI > SYNC > CLK IN on.
  • A computer over USB (macOS): notes, CCs, and MIDI LEARN with an M-VAVE SMC Mixer in MIDI mode.

MIDI LEARN

Black key 4 turns MIDI LEARN on or off (lit while on; the screen reads MIDI LEARN). The EDIT pages and the effects' pages then show, in each row, the CC learned for it, or — if none. PRESETS chooses the row; OCT− / OCT+ turn the pages.

ToDo this
Learn a CCSAVE (WAIT shows), then move the control: the next CC to arrive, on any channel, is learned
Stop waitingSAVE again
Forget the row's CCSHIFT + SAVE

A learned sound parameter moves on the track it was learned on; an effect's moves for all. Each CC and channel controls one parameter, and each parameter has one CC. Up to 64 are kept, with GLOBAL SETUP. RECEIVE CC must be on.

USB audio

Plugged into a computer, a phone or a tablet, the FM-1 is also a USB audio input named FM-1 Bigorna: its master output in stereo, 16-bit, 44.1 kHz. Record or monitor it like any class-compliant audio interface; nothing to install. The headphone jack plays on as usual. The USB sound does not follow the MASTER knob, so a recording keeps its level whatever the headphones are set to. MIDI goes on alongside on the same cable.

The other end must be a USB host: a computer, or a phone or tablet that takes USB audio devices (on Android, most do through USB-C). A host that works at 48 kHz converts the sound itself.

Tested with:

  • POCO X7 Pro (HyperOS), over USB-C: the phone's camera app records video with the FM-1's sound. Switch on OTG first (Settings > Additional settings > OTG), with nothing plugged into the phone; HyperOS turns it off again after 10 minutes with no device.
  • MacBook Air M5 (macOS), over USB-C: FM-1 Bigorna, 2 input channels, 44,100 Hz, every packet in order with six tracks playing.

The screen

Few words, very large type, high contrast, and a colour for each track. The track's view shows, from the top: the pattern playing (orange with changes not saved) and the chord form (or ARP) at the top left; the battery, the octave and the transposition (T+2) at the top right, with REC or LOOP while recording; the track's number, its machine and its sound's family.

The battery shows three green bars when full, then two green, one amber, and one red when it runs low. On USB power it shows a white bolt instead.

Rescue

Hold OCT− while switching the FM-1 on for the rescue screen, from which the installer can run again; two failed starts in a row also lead there. If the FM-1 starts but no longer answers over USB, hold OCT− and OCT+ for 5 seconds while it runs: the chip's own update mode, from which a firmware can be restored with Melodee's recovery tool.
